title: Testicular Torsion and Acute Scrotum: Emergency Assessment and Surgical Referral

evidenceAudit.scope: Boys and men with acute scrotal pain or swelling in the emergency department (ED) or primary care: recognising testicular torsion, immediate surgical referral, role and limits of Doppler ultrasound, differentials (torsion of the appendix testis, epididymo-orchitis, irreducible hernia, idiopathic scrotal oedema) and disposition. Uses the European Association of Urology (EAU) paediatric urology guideline and the Royal Children's Hospital (RCH) Melbourne 2026 guideline. Adult torsion follows the same surgical urgency.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-22.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi acute scrotum guideline was found.
The EAU chapter is paediatric; its urgency is applied to adults by extension.
Neither source gives analgesic doses; analgesia follows the local acute pain protocol.
Antibiotic choice for epididymo-orchitis is not given by these sources.
The publication year of the EAU chapter was not shown on the page opened.
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.

pathophysiology.summary: Torsion twists the spermatic cord and cuts the testicular blood supply; the critical window for salvage is about 4 to 6 hours (EAU acute scrotum, Section 8.2). Torsion peaks in the newborn period and around puberty (EAU acute scrotum, Section 8.1). Perinatal torsion most often happens before birth (EAU acute scrotum, Section 8.1). Torsion of the appendix testis causes focal pain at the upper pole and is managed without surgery once confirmed (EAU acute scrotum, Section 8.2 and Recommendations).

symptoms: Sudden severe scrotal pain, which may spread to the groin, iliac fossa or thigh (RCH acute scrotum 2026, Section Assessment).
Nausea and vomiting in about 90% (RCH acute scrotum 2026, Section Assessment; EAU acute scrotum, Section 8.2).
Neonates may show no pain, only scrotal discolouration (RCH acute scrotum 2026, Section Assessment).
Fever, dysuria or discharge point more to epididymo-orchitis (RCH acute scrotum 2026, Section Differentials).
physicalSigns: High-riding or horizontal testis (EAU acute scrotum, Section 8.2; RCH acute scrotum 2026, Section Assessment).
Absent cremasteric reflex (EAU acute scrotum, Section 8.2).
Tender testis with thickened cord; red or blue scrotal skin (RCH acute scrotum 2026, Section Assessment).
Isolated upper-pole tenderness or blue dot sign in appendix torsion (EAU acute scrotum, Section 8.2; RCH acute scrotum 2026, Section Differentials).
redFlags: Suspected torsion at any age: immediate surgical review; do not delay for tests (RCH acute scrotum 2026, Section Key points; EAU acute scrotum, Recommendations).
Irreducible inguinal hernia: urgent surgical review (RCH acute scrotum 2026, Section Key points).
Scrotal bruising in an infant or with an unclear story: consider child abuse (RCH acute scrotum 2026, Section Key points).
Pain for more than 4 to 6 hours: testicular loss risk rises (EAU acute scrotum, Section 8.2).
precipitants: Puberty and the neonatal period (EAU acute scrotum, Section 8.1).
Previous intermittent scrotal pain (EAU acute scrotum, Section 8.2).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Age 7 to 12, focal upper-pole tenderness, blue dot; conservative care once torsion is excluded (RCH acute scrotum 2026, Section Differentials; EAU acute scrotum, Recommendations).
Fever, dysuria or discharge, tender posterolateral epididymis; antibiotics (RCH acute scrotum 2026, Section Differentials; EAU acute scrotum, Section 8.2).
Infant with firm tender swelling that will not reduce (RCH acute scrotum 2026, Section Differentials).
Age 3 to 7, purplish swelling spreading to perineum or groin; resolves in 1 to 5 days (RCH acute scrotum 2026, Section Differentials).
Scrotal vasculitis with typical rash (RCH acute scrotum 2026, Section Differentials).

clinicalManagement.title: Assess quickly
actions: Take onset, nausea, urinary symptoms and trauma history; examine testis lie, cremasteric reflex, cord and upper pole (EAU acute scrotum, Section 8.2; RCH acute scrotum 2026, Section Assessment).
Keep nil by mouth or sips of clear fluid until surgical review (RCH acute scrotum 2026, Section When to call surgeons).
Give adequate analgesia per the local acute pain protocol (RCH acute scrotum 2026, Section Analgesia).

clinicalManagement.title: Call surgery immediately
clinicalManagement.timeframe: Immediately if torsion cannot be excluded
actions: Consult the surgical or urology team urgently in every case where torsion cannot be confidently excluded (RCH acute scrotum 2026, Section When to call surgeons).
Do not wait for ultrasound or blood tests (RCH acute scrotum 2026, Section Key points; EAU acute scrotum, Recommendations).
Transfer if surgery is not available locally (RCH acute scrotum 2026, Section Disposition).

clinicalManagement.title: Manual detorsion while waiting
actions: Manual detorsion may be tried while awaiting theatre but must not delay surgery (EAU acute scrotum, Section 8.3.2).

clinicalManagement.title: Surgery
clinicalManagement.timeframe: As soon as possible, ideally within 4 to 6 hours
actions: Urgent exploration for all torsion within 24 hours of onset; semi-elective after 24 hours (EAU acute scrotum, Section 8.3.3).
Contralateral orchidopexy is commonly done when torsion is confirmed; in neonates, fix the other testis (EAU acute scrotum, Section 8.3.2 and Recommendations).

clinicalManagement.title: If torsion excluded
actions: Appendix torsion: rest and analgesia; pain settles in 5 to 10 days (RCH acute scrotum 2026, Section Differentials).
Epididymo-orchitis: antibiotics, intravenous if unwell or a young infant; renal tract ultrasound and urology review after a second episode (RCH acute scrotum 2026, Section Differentials).

medicationPlan.note: No disease-specific drug. Give analgesia by the local acute pain protocol and antibiotics for epididymo-orchitis by local guidance; neither source gives doses (RCH acute scrotum 2026, Sections Analgesia and Differentials). diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Base the diagnosis on physical examination (EAU acute scrotum, Recommendations; strong).
All suspected torsion as soon as possible, ideally within 4 to 6 hours and within 24 hours of onset; semi-elective after 24 hours (EAU acute scrotum, Section 8.3.3 and Recommendations).
The Testicular Workup for Ischemia and Suspected Torsion (TWIST) score should not be relied on alone (EAU acute scrotum, Section 8.2).

teaching.scope: Boys and men with acute scrotal pain or swelling in the emergency department (ED) or primary care: recognising testicular torsion, immediate surgical referral, role and limits of Doppler ultrasound, differentials (torsion of the appendix testis, epididymo-orchitis, irreducible hernia, idiopathic scrotal oedema) and disposition. Uses the European Association of Urology (EAU) paediatric urology guideline and the Royal Children's Hospital (RCH) Melbourne 2026 guideline. Adult torsion follows the same surgical urgency.
learningObjectives: Call surgeons immediately without waiting for ultrasound.
Know the 4 to 6 hour salvage window.
Separate appendix torsion, epididymo-orchitis and hernia.
pitfalls: Sending for ultrasound before surgical review.
Diagnosing epididymitis in a vomiting teenager without fever.
Missing torsion in a neonate with a discoloured scrotum.
keyPoints: Absent cremasteric reflex is very sensitive for torsion.
Normal Doppler flow does not exclude torsion.
Nausea and vomiting are common in torsion.

patientEducation: Sudden severe testicle pain is an emergency; come to hospital at once.
After surgery, report fever, wound redness or new pain.
lifestyleAndDiet: Rest and scrotal support after surgery or appendix torsion.
mdtReferrals: Emergency physician; paediatric surgeon or urologist; anaesthetist; paediatric team for safeguarding concerns (RCH acute scrotum 2026, Section Key points).
dischargeCriteria: Torsion excluded or treated, pain controlled, surgical advice and follow-up plan in place (RCH acute scrotum 2026, Section Disposition).
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Surgical follow-up after exploration; urology review after a second epididymo-orchitis episode (RCH acute scrotum 2026, Sections Disposition and Differentials).
